item.title: A generalization of the Dirichlet approximation theorem for affine actions on the real line
item.description: arXiv:2611.03778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quantitative density of orbits of the free semigroup $\Gamma$ generated by two maps of $(0,\infty)$. For the M\"obius pair $x\mapsto 1/x$, $x\mapsto x+1$ we show that every orbit is $O(n^{-1})$-dense in $[0,\infty)$, that every irrational number $u$ is approached at a rate governed by the continued fraction of $u$ (at least $n^{-2}$, exponential when $u$ has bounded partial quotients, and $\exp(-cn/\log n)$ for almost every $u$), and that for rational $u$ and rational starting points the rate $n^{-1}$ is optimal. For the affine pair $T_0(x)=x/a$, $T_1(x)=bx+1$ with $a,b>1$, which was studied by Bergelson, Misiurewicz and Senti, we prove that for every $x>0$ and $u\ge 0$ there are infinitely many $\gamma\in\Gamma$ with \[ |\gamma(x)-u|<C\,\lambda^{-|\gamma|},\qquad \lambda=\exp\!\Big(\frac{\log a\,\log\frac{a}{a-1}}{\log\frac{a^2b}{a-1}}\Big)>1, \] where $|\gamma|$ is the word length of $\gamma$ and $C$ is independent of $\gamma$. This exponential rate holds whether or not $\log_a b$ is rational, and the exponential order cannot be improved for almost every $u$. We also give a corrected version of the Kronecker-type estimate $|\gamma(x)-u|<(u+1)(t^{1/|\gamma|}-1)$. Finally, we discuss the approximation of real numbers by ratios of primes and by ratios of logarithms of primes, updated in light of recent results on gaps between primes.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, A generalization of Dirichlet approximation theorem for the affine actions on real line, J. Number Theory 128 (2008), no. 5, 1146--1156
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over sextic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.03933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine all the groups that appear as the torsion group of an elliptic curve over a number field of degree $6$. Apart from the $44$ groups that occur infinitely often, which were determined by Derickx and Sutherland, exactly four groups occur: $\mathbb{Z}/25\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/12\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$. The first three were known to occur, while the group $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ is new. We also show that, up to isomorphism, each of the groups $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ is the torsion group of a single elliptic curve over a single sextic field. The methods build on those developed by Derickx and Najman for quartic fields and by the author for quintic fields. Among the new ingredients are a formal immersion criterion at the prime $2$ which uses the Cartier operator, and arguments with several diamond operators and with cuspidal divisor classes on quotients of modular curves.
item.dc:creator: Filip Najman

item.title: Some instances of modularity for residually reducible representations in the mixed case
item.description: arXiv:2611.04017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field, abelian over $\Q$, in which an odd prime $p$ splits completely, and let $\rho:G_F\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_p)$ be an odd irreducible representation which is de Rham with distinct Hodge--Tate weights at the places above $p$ and whose residual representation is reducible. We consider the \emph{mixed} case of the Fontaine--Mazur conjecture, in which $\rho$ is reducible at some places above $p$ and irreducible at the others. This case is not covered by the work of Pan and Zhang. We prove some instances of modularity in this situation. Our main result is that $\rho$ is modular if it is non-split at every place above $p$ where it is reducible, by combining Zhang's pro-modularity theorem with a classicality criterion based on Emerton's ordinary parts. Together with a theorem of Zhao on local indecomposability, this gives the modularity of the $\lambda$-adic representations attached to abelian varieties of $\GL_2$-type in the mixed case, and, using a result of Snowden, of potentially modular representations of parallel weight two under a mild additional condition. It also gives the modularity of representations whose local type at every place above $p$ is of discrete series type, and, through a member of the compatible system with interchanged Hodge-Tate weights, of potentially modular representations of weight $(2,k)$ over real quadratic fields with Steinberg type at one place above $p$, under conditions on that member.
item.dc:creator: Luis V. Dieulefait

item.title: Ramanujan-type congruences for the smallest parts function
item.description: arXiv:2611.04178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a famous paper of Andrews, he defined and studied the smallest parts function $\operatorname{spt}(n)$. He showed that it satisfies the three Ramanujan-type congruences: \[ \operatorname{spt}(5n+4)\equiv0\pmod5,\qquad \operatorname{spt}(7n+5)\equiv0\pmod7,\qquad \operatorname{spt}(13n+6)\equiv0\pmod{13}. \] In a recent preprint, the author showed that these are the only "canonical'' congruences. Here, we complete the classification of Ramanujan-type congruences for $\operatorname{spt}$, showing that if $\operatorname{spt}(\ell n+b)\equiv0\pmod\ell$ for all $n\geq0$, where $\ell\geq5$ is prime, then $(\ell,b)\in\{(5,4),(7,5),(13,6)\}.$ That is, Andrews' congruences are the only Ramanujan-type congruences for $\operatorname{spt}(n)$. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Larry Rolen

item.title: Rational points on loxodromic K3 surfaces and complex dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.04210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an analogue of the Hilbert irreducibility theorem for all K3 surfaces over number fields that admit an automorphism of positive entropy. Our method draws ingredients from both algebraic geometry and complex dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Dami\'an Gvirtz-Chen, Zhizhong Huang, Zhuchao Ji, Junyi Xie

item.title: On integers $n$ relatively prime to $\lfloor \alpha n^2\rfloor$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ and $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S_{\alpha,k}(x):=\#\{n\in\mathbb N:n\le x,\ \gcd(n,\lfloor\alpha n^k\rfloor)=1\}$. Roth conjectured, and Watson proved, that $S_{\alpha,1}(x)\sim 6x/\pi^2$ for every irrational $\alpha$. Whether the same asymptotic holds for every fixed $k\ge2$ is a special case of a question of Bergelson and Richter, and was asked explicitly by Champagne. We answer this for $k=2$, with no Diophantine condition on $\alpha$: for every irrational $\alpha$, $S_{\alpha,2}(x)\sim x/\zeta(2)$ as $x\to\infty$. More precisely, for every fixed $A>0$ we obtain an error term $O_A(x/(\log q(x))^A)$, where $q(x)$ is the largest continued-fraction convergent denominator of $\alpha$ not exceeding $x$. The proof sieves $S_{\alpha,2}(x)$ over divisors, splitting at the parameter $R=q(x)^{1/8}$. Divisors larger than $R$ are handled by reducing the condition $d\mid\gcd(n,\lfloor\alpha n^2\rfloor)$ to M\"obius sums over arithmetic progressions and applying Zhan's uniform estimate for exponential sums twisted by $\mu(n)$ over short intervals; divisors at most $R$ are handled instead through the Erd\H{o}s-Tur\'an inequality together with Weyl-type bounds for quadratic exponential sums of the form $\sum e(\beta n^2)$.
item.dc:creator: Aahan Chatterjee

item.title: The smallest-parts function and elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.04387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, Ono established a new connection between partition congruences and the arithmetic of elliptic curves by expressing the partition function $p(n)$ as a CM trace on the modular curve $X_0(6)$. This approach yields new proofs of Ramanujan-type congruences for the partition function modulo powers of $5$, $7$, and $11$, revealing how the geometry of supersingular elliptic curves and the arithmetic of oriented optimal embeddings govern these congruence properties. Motivated by Ono's work, we develop an analogous passage from CM traces to congruences modulo $5$, $7$, and $13$ for the for Andrews's smallest-parts partition function $spt(n)$, employing the established theta-lift and modular-trace methods suited to this setting. With $P$ the Bruinier--Ono weight-zero weak Maass function and $f$ an explicit weakly holomorphic modular function on $\Gamma_0(6)$, the Ahlgren--Andersen formula expresses $spt(n)$ as one twelfth of the discriminant $1-24n$ CM trace of $f-P$. We explain the theta-lift normalization, the contribution of the two orientations, and the harmonic-Maass-form uniqueness argument. Following Garvan's work, we construct integral forms $G_\ell$ of weight $\ell+1$ on $\Gamma_0(\ell)$, compute their Fricke transformations, and prove the exact identities $$ \mathcal T_5(G_5)=-5E_6,\qquad \mathcal T_7(G_7)=-7E_8,\qquad \mathcal T_{13}(G_{13})=13E_{14}. $$ Their reductions yield the three congruences on the Andrews's smallest-parts partition function. We also give a supersingular specialization of the trace of $f$, with actual reduction multiplicities, and explain the role of imprimitive forms, the conductor restriction in CM reduction, and the distinction between the primes $11$ and $13$. These results have been verified in Lean using AxiomProver.
item.dc:creator: Ajit Singh

item.title: Finding Integer Roots of Polynomials in Nearly Optimal Time
item.description: arXiv:2611.04730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients of absolute value less than $2^b$. Using Pan's approximate factorization theorem, we give a deterministic algorithm that finds all distinct integer roots of $f$ in $\widetilde O(nb)$ bit operations. This matches the bit size of the input up to logarithmic factors and does not require $f$ to be square-free. Since we were unable to verify parts of the running time analysis of Pan's theorem, we also give a self-contained deterministic algorithm with running time $\widetilde O(nb+\min(n,b)^3b^2)$, which is $\widetilde O(nb)$ whenever $b\leq n^{1/4}$. This answers a question of Harvey and Hittmeir (2022), who asked whether integer roots can be found deterministically in quasilinear time, conditionally on Pan's theorem, and unconditionally for $b\leq n^{1/4}$. The fastest previous deterministic algorithm, due to Nir, takes $\widetilde O(n^{3/2}b)$ bit operations and works only for square-free polynomials. Instead of $p$-adic lifting, we combine approximate complex root finding with exact polynomial evaluation. We first approximate the complex roots of the polynomial formed by the top $\min(n,b)+1$ coefficients of $f$. Every integer root $r$ of $f$ with $|r|\geq 2$ lies within distance $2$ of some complex root of this truncated polynomial. Rounding the real parts of the approximate roots therefore gives a list of $O(\min(n,b))$ candidate integers that is guaranteed to contain all integer roots of $f$. Although a single candidate can have up to $b$ bits, a bound via the Mahler measure shows that the bit lengths of all candidates sum to $O(b)$. This allows us to test all candidates by exact multipoint evaluation in $\widetilde O(nb)$ bit operations.
item.dc:creator: Yansong Feng, Itamar Nir

item.title: Counting irreducible skew polynomials $x^{2n}+ax^n+1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a counting formula for the coefficients $a\in\F_{p^h}$ for which $x^{2n}+ax^n+1$ is irreducible in $\F_{p^h}[x;\sigma]$, for arbitrary positive integers $n$ and $h$, where $\sigma(a)=a^p$ and $p$ is an arbitrary prime power. The proof reduces the problem to quadratic reduced norms, establishes a uniformity statement for every Frobenius generator, and counts the remaining coefficients by M\"obius inversion.
item.dc:creator: Tomoya Hayata, Takahiro Tsushima

item.title: Inverse powers and 2-adic properties of binary 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci sequence
item.description: arXiv:2611.04855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study binary 3 x 3 matrices with determinant one that generate the Tribonacci recurrence. Starting from a specific generating matrix, we obtain explicit expressions for its powers and inverse powers in terms of the Tribonacci sequence T_n and two associated sequences B_n and R_n. This matrix framework yields identities involving traces, determinants, and products, including addition formulas and Cassini-type relations linking T_n, B_n, and Rn. Moreover, we derive new identities from the matrix representation of inverse powers and establish structural relations between these sequences. As an application, we investigate arithmetic properties of Tribonacci numbers and determine the exact 2-adic valuation of T_2^k for sufficiently large k. Finally, we provide a classification of 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci recurrence via similarity over Q.
item.dc:creator: Wilson Arley Martinez, Samin Ingrith Ceron

item.title: Asymptotics for partitions over the Fibonacci numbers and related sequences, II
item.description: arXiv:2611.04869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a recent paper of the same title, we considered nondistinct partitions of integers over the Fibonacci sequence and related linearly recurrent sequences. In this paper, continuing this story, we apply the same method, but consider distinct partitions. In particular, let $q_F(m)$ denote the number of ways of writing $m$ as the sum of distinct Fibonacci numbers. It is well-known that, while $q_F(m)$ behaves wildly, its partial sums behave in a more structured way. In particular, Kempton showed that the function $N^{-\log 2/\log\varphi}\sum_{m\leqslant N}q_F(m)$ is asymptotically logarithmically-periodic. In this paper, we improve on this result by providing an explicit error term. Additionally, we prove the analogous result for a class of more general linear recurrent sequences.
item.dc:creator: Michael Coons, Simon Kristensen, Mathias L. Laursen

item.title: On the Diophantine equation $Cx^2+p_1^{2m_1}p_2^{2m_2}\cdots p_k^{2m_k}=y^q$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C>3$ be an odd square-free integer, $q$ an odd prime not dividing the class number of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-C})$, and $p_1,\dots,p_k$ distinct odd primes not dividing $C$. We describe all solutions of $Cx^2+p_1^{2m_1}\cdots p_k^{2m_k}=y^q$ in positive integers with $\gcd(x,y)=1$ and $y$ odd. Writing $N=p_1^{m_1}\cdots p_k^{m_k}$, every solution comes from a unique factorization $x\sqrt C+N\sqrt{-1}=\pm(u\sqrt C\pm v\sqrt{-1})^q$, or from a half-integral analogue when $q=3$, in which each $p_i\ne q$ divides exactly one of $v$ and $N/v$. Using primitive divisors of Lehmer sequences, we show that for $q\ge5$ some $p_i$ satisfies $p_i\equiv\leg{-C}{p_i}\pmod q$; in particular, there is no solution when $q\ge\max(5,p_1+2,\dots,p_k+2)$. For $q=3$ the equation reduces to four explicit auxiliary equations.
item.dc:creator: Usha K. Sangale, Priyanka R. Satpute

item.title: Almost primes in short intervals and averages of long Dirichlet polynomial approximations to $(\zeta'/\zeta)^{k}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.05000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the mean square of long truncations of the Dirichlet series for $\bigl(\zeta'/\zeta\bigr)^{k}$ on the critical line; we establish the connection between this problem and the short-interval variance of the convoluted von Mangoldt function $\Lambda^{*k}$ in short intervals and in arithmetic progressions. Under a shifted moments conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), we prove that the short-interval variance leading coefficient is the derivative of the mean-square leading coefficient. A unitary trace-sum average governs the variance of sums of $\Lambda^{*k}$ over monic polynomials in $\mathbb F_q[T]$; we denote its leading coefficient by $\delta_k(c)$, where the total trace degree and matrix size grow with a fixed ratio $c$. Under a weaker shifted moments conjecture and RH, we recover this $\delta_k(c)$ as the leading coefficient of the variance of short-interval sums of $\Lambda^{*k}$ over the integers. It is the counterpart of $\gamma_k(c)$, the piecewise polynomial from the variance of divisor sums, with the Dirichlet coefficients of $\zeta(s)^k$ replaced by those of $\bigl(-\zeta'/\zeta\bigr)^k$.
item.dc:creator: Siegfred Baluyot, John Brian Conrey, Ayesha Irfan, Nina C. Snaith

item.title: On partitions with bounded multiplicity restrictions on even parts and with the largest part being odd
item.description: arXiv:2611.05160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Andrews and El Bachraoui (\textit{RACSAM} \textbf{119}, \textit{Article Number 4 (2025)}) established identities relating $4$-regular partitions to partitions with distinct even parts whose largest part is odd. As an extension to their work, in this paper we define partitions of a positive integer $n$ with bounded multiplicity restriction on even parts and whose largest part is odd. We prove some identities relating our partition functions and $2r$-regular partition function, and show that identities due to Andrews and El Bachraoui follow as particular cases.
item.dc:creator: Gaurab Bardhan, Nipen Saikia

item.title: Divisibility Properties of Odd Part and Even Part Sums in Cubic Partitions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A cubic partition of a positive integer $n$ is a partition of $n$ in which even parts may appear in two distinct colors. The purpose of this paper is to study the arithmetic functions $COS(n)$ and $CES(n)$, which denote the sums of all odd and even parts, respectively, in all cubic partitions of $n$. We obtain their generating functions and divisor-sum formulas, and establish Ramanujan-type congruences modulo $3$, $4$, $5$, and $7$. To prove these congruences, we use Lambert series, classical theta-function identities, dissections, coefficient extraction, and weighted Euler identities.
item.dc:creator: Gaurab Bardhan, Nipen Saikia

item.title: On the van der Corput property for cubes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a power-saving form of the van der Corput property for cubes. As a consequence, we obtain a power-saving bound $|A|\ll_\varepsilon N^{59/60+\varepsilon}$ for sets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonzero cube differences.
item.dc:creator: Steve Fan, Andrew Lott, \'Akos Magyar, M\'at\'e Matolcsi, Imre Z. Ruzsa

item.title: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
item.description: arXiv:2611.02515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincar\'e expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a punctured surface times a circle, by gluing solid tori to its boundary tori, and we place a copy of the Narain theory on each of these tori. The ensemble average supplies the sum over the solid tori, or more precisely over marked presentations with fixed base genus, number of fibers and integer Seifert invariant. The resulting sum converges absolutely and is a polynomial in the components of the vector-valued Eisenstein series. When all the boundary tori share a single modulus, the average acquires connected corrections, which we identify with wormholes gluing the core to itself; for two boundary tori, the terms with rational Lagrangian sublattices of the Siegel-Eisenstein series are realized by wormholes containing an exceptional fiber. After reduction along the fiber, the construction closely parallels the two-dimensional topological gravity of Marolf and Maxfield, with the base of the fibration playing the role of their spacetime. We also discuss Dehn fillings of 3-manifolds with torus boundary, non-orientable bases, and the surgery formula. Our results suggest that modularity could be an organizing principle in the summation of geometries in quantum gravity.
item.dc:creator: Kei Kaneda, Masahito Yamazaki

item.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04514v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $\rho$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)$ is the $\rho(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $\Pi(\rho)$ under Scholze's functor, and $\Pi(\rho)$ is the representation associated to $\rho$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.
item.dc:creator: Yu Xiao

item.title: Good slopes, congruence preservation, and gaps over residue rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.04551v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We call $f$ congruence-preserving if it preserves congruences modulo every divisor of $n$. For odd prime powers $n$, we classify all permutations with more than $n/2$ good slopes. Among permutations that are not congruence-preserving, we determine the maximum number of good slopes for $n=3^e$ with $e\ge2$, and for $n=25$, $125$ and $625$. Every permutation of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ has at most $\varphi(n)$ good slopes, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. For several families of moduli with at least two distinct prime divisors, we prove a sharp upper bound for the number of good slopes of the permutations with fewer than $\varphi(n)$ good slopes. These families include $9q$ and $3q^e$ for every prime $q\ge5$ and every $e\ge1$. Together with a companion paper, this settles the bound for every odd composite modulus below $105$.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K. Bhunia

item.title: Polynomial configurations and pointwise averages along Piatetski--Shapiro primes
item.description: arXiv:2611.04575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every \(c>1\) sufficiently close to \(1\), we prove that there is \(\kappa>0\) such that every sufficiently large \(A\subset[N]\) of density at least \((\log N)^{-\kappa}\) contains \[ x,\ x+(p-1),\ x+(p-1)^2,\ldots,\ x+(p-1)^k, \qquad p=\lfloor n^c\rfloor\in\mathbb P. \] We also prove pointwise almost-everywhere convergence of the corresponding multiple ergodic averages.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Mousavi

item.title: Additive energy, Freiman's lemma, and an edge-isoperimetric problem on the boolean cube
item.description: arXiv:2611.04644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite, non-empty set not contained in any translate of a hyperplane. We show that there exists a subset $S \subseteq A$ such that $d \ll |S| \ll d$ and \[E(A,S) := |\{(a_1,a_2,s_1,s_2)\in A\times A\times S\times S:a_1+s_1=a_2+s_2\}|\ll\lvert A\rvert\lvert S\rvert.\] This can be interpreted as a robust, analytic generalisation of the classical Freiman's lemma, and recovers Freiman's lemma up to a constant multiplicative factor. In the process of proving this result, we also show that for any integer $1 \leq m \leq d$ and any set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $|A| \leq \binom{d}{m}$, one has \[ E(A, B) \leq 4(m + 1/m) |A||B|,\] where $B$ is the canonical basis of $\mathbb{Z}^d$. This gives new estimates for multiplicative energies between finite sets of primes and arbitrary subsets of positive integers, improving a previous result of Shkredov. Using related ideas, we also prove new bounds for an edge-isoperimetric problem for certain graphs on the boolean cube, improving an earlier result of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky. We give two different proofs of the first result described in this abstract and three different proofs of the second one.
item.dc:creator: Akshat Mudgal, Carl Schildkraut, Dmitrii Zakharov

item.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
item.description: arXiv:2611.04773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $\Lambda=\pi_1^{alg}(G)$, the Galois group $\Theta=Gal(L/K)$ acting on $\Lambda$, where $L$ is a finite Galois extension of $K$ having no real places, the decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v\subseteq \Theta$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $\Theta_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. We also compute $Sha^S(K,G)$ in some cases where $S$ contains archimedean places.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Borovoi

item.title: Hecke Relations from Self-Duality
item.description: arXiv:2611.05002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hecke operators can be used to relate characters of rational conformal field theories with different central charges, but it has remained a mystery how to interpret these relations physically. We offer a simple explanation in terms of self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds. Self-dual orbifolds also give more general identities beyond the familiar Harvey-Wu construction, which we illustrate through examples.
item.dc:creator: Justin Kaidi

item.title: On the $abc$ conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.05217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using adelic intersection theory and following the method envisioned by Parshin and Moret-Bailly, we prove a conjecture of Vojta for curves of genus two and a weak form of the $abc$ conjecture
item.dc:creator: Christophe Soul\'e

item.title: Harmonic analysis approach to the relative Riemann-Roch theorem on global fields
item.description: arXiv:2208.10424v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we generalize and put in a new light part of ``Fouier analysis on Number fields and Hecke's zeta function''[14] by Tate. We express the relative Euler characteristic using purely adelic language. By using certain natural normalization of Haar measure on adeles we obtain the relative Riemann-Roch theorem. In particular we show that using our relative normalization of the Haar measure on adeles we can obtain the relative Riemann-Roch theorem from the adelic Poisson summation formulae. In addition, using our methods we define the relative 'size of cohomology' numbers, i.e. extract the $h^0$ and $h^1$ part of the relative Euler characteristic. Our theory not only covers both absolute and relative cases, but also the case of an arithmetic curve and a nonsingular, projective curve over a finite field.
item.dc:creator: Weronika Czerniawska

item.title: The prime geodesic theorem for the modular orbifold
item.description: arXiv:2402.12133v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the prime geodesic theorem for the modular orbifold with exponent $\frac{9}{13} = 0.692307 \cdots$ in the error term. By periodicity and Heath-Brown's quadratic large sieve, we estimate the sixth moment of the error term in an approximation to the Zagier $L$-series at $s = 1$. The smooth explicit formula of Soundararajan and Young then leads to the stated exponent without recourse to subconvexity for quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: Ikuya Kaneko

item.title: Dwork Motives, Monodromy and Potential Automorphy
item.description: arXiv:2407.16481v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study certain families of motives, which arise as direct summands of the cohomology of the Dwork family. We computationally find examples of interesting families with the following three properties. Firstly, their geometric monodromy group is Zariski dense in $\operatorname{SL}_n$. Secondly, they realise many different unipotent operators as the monodromy operator at $t = \infty$. Thirdly, all their Hodge numbers are $\leq 1$. This has consequences for Galois representations. Namely, if a nilpotent operator $N$ appears as the monodromy at $t = \infty$ in one of our families, we can construct potentially automorphic representations with $\ell$-adic monodromy given by $N$ at a fixed prime $p$. As another application, we obtain a new proof of some cases of the recent local-global compatibility theorem of Matsumoto.
item.dc:creator: Lambert A'Campo

item.title: R\'epartition conjointe de trois nombres premiers et applications
item.description: arXiv:2410.02480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove asymptotic results for the singular series associated to the distribution of three primes. Assuming a quantitative version of Hardy and Littlewood's conjecture on prime 3-tuples, we deduce an asymptotic formula related to the joint distribution of three primes. This improves recent results of Kuperberg and completes results by Montgomery and Soundararajan. Following the Montgomery and Soundararajan approach, we derive conjectural applications to the distribution of primes in short intervals.
item.dc:creator: R\'egis de la Bret\`eche

item.title: A boundary example for the Volterra decomposition of arithmetic error terms
item.description: arXiv:2601.11052v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let phi(n) denote the Euler totient function. We study the analytic part associated with the summatory function of sigma_1(n) and obtain explicit bounds under the Riemann Hypothesis. In particular, we establish an upper bound of order x^{delta'} exp((log x)/(log log x)), where delta' = max(1/2, delta).
item.dc:creator: Hideto Iwata

item.title: Fields with no everywhere good abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2603.17708v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend methods of Fontaine, Abrashkin and Schoof to obtain criteria determining number fields K over which no non-zero abelian variety with everywhere good reduction exists. As an application, under the GRH, we find 26847 such fields of various degrees up to 16.
item.dc:creator: Armand Brumer, Kenneth Kramer

item.title: Functoriality and the theta correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2604.03095v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the functoriality of the local theta correspondence for classical $p$-adic groups. This is realized via the adaptation of the Adams conjecture to ABV-packets. We provide evidence for the conjecture, especially in the case of general linear groups.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hazeltine

item.title: Hal\'asz theorems for Gaussian ideals in sectors and short intervals
item.description: arXiv:2605.19105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a quantitative Hal\'asz theorem for multiplicative functions on the nonzero ideals of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, with bounds controlled by pretentious distance to the Archimedean characters $N^{it}$. We also prove a sectorial analogue: under angular non-pretentiousness, the sum of $f$ over ideals lying in a fixed sector is asymptotically given by the expected proportion of the unrestricted sum. Finally, under angular non-pretentiousness and a non-degeneracy condition on conjugate prime pairs, we prove a sectorial short-interval version of the Hal\'asz theorem for annular sectors whose radial thickness tends to infinity. The proof of the sectorial short-interval Hal\'asz theorem uses angular Fourier expansion, norm-compression to multiplicative functions on $\mathbb{N}$, and a theorem of Mangerel.
item.dc:creator: Jan Ku\'s

item.title: Integrality of height-one formal groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.25726v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove that a one-dimensional formal group law over $K$ has integral coefficients if and only if its multiplication-by-$n$ endomorphisms have integral coefficients for all integers $n$, in the height-one case, that is when the multiplication by $p$ has Weierstrass degree $p$. The proof relies on $p$-adic Hodge theory.
item.dc:creator: Martin Debaisieux

item.title: The $\beta=2$ partition function of Dirichlet $L$-functions and typical maxima
item.description: arXiv:2608.09906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the $\beta=2$ partition function $\int_{|h| \leq \log ^{\theta} q/2}|L(1/2+ih,\chi)|^2dh$ for typical Dirichlet characters modulo a large prime $q$ and $\theta \in (-1/3,0]$ motivated by a $q$-analogue of the Saksman--Webb conjectures. When $\theta <0$, we use an extension of Harper's randomisation argument with different localisations to recover moment upper bounds consistent with the critical normalisation predicted there. As an application, we prove that for $q(1-o(1))$ Dirichlet characters modulo $q$ with $U(q) \to \infty$, $$\max_{|h| \leq 1/2}|L(1/2+ih,\chi)|\ll \frac{e^{U(q)}\log q\log_3 q(\log_4 q)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 q)^{3/4}},$$ establishing an upper bound matching the predictions of the $q$-analogue of the Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating conjectures up to second order. Our proofs adapt Harper's argument in \cite{harper2019partition}.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Atherfold

item.title: Intersective Polynomials and Universal Separation of Divosor Profiles
item.description: arXiv:2608.13388v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify universal divisor-profile separation for coprime polynomial pairs of arbitrary degree and for all pairs of degree at most two. For \(A\subset\N\) and \(m\in\Z\), let \(d_A(m)\) count the members of \(A\) dividing \(m\). For coprime nonzero \(F,G\in\Z[x]\), universally unbounded separation between \(d_A(F(n))\) and \(d_A(G(n))\) occurs if and only if one of \(F,G\) is intersective, that is, has a root modulo every positive integer. More generally, an intersective factor separated from finitely many polynomial opponents yields simultaneous one-sided dominance against all of them. For pairs with common irreducible factors, let \(U,V\) be the products of the factors occurring only on the two respective sides. Universal separation forces \(UV\) to have a root modulo almost every prime; equivalently, its Galois action has no derangement. We resolve the remaining finite \(p\)-adic boundary for all pairs of degree at most two: separation holds exactly when \(UV\) and at least one of \(F,G\) are intersective, and the criterion is unchanged by contents or factor multiplicities. The same criterion holds, in arbitrary degree, for three linear support factors with arbitrary positive multiplicities. The proofs combine uniform almost-prime values on root progressions with an adaptive local-routing argument.
item.dc:creator: Zihan Zhang

item.title: $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the Bogomolov property for canonical heights
item.description: arXiv:2609.24938v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that for any number field $K$ and any rational map $f$ in $K(x)$ of degree at least $2$ that is not conjugate to a power, (signed) Chebyshev or CM Latt\`es map, $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the strong Bogomolov property for the canonical height of $f$. Combined with former results of Amoroso-Zannier, Pottmeyer and Ratazzi, this implies that $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has the Bogomolov property for canonical heights of any rational map of degree at least $2$. We also classify the pairs $(f,\alpha)$ whose backward orbit contains infinitely many abelian points. This settles the Andrews--Petsche conjecture in the greater generality of rational maps over a number field and infinite abelian subsets of backward orbits. The authors were led to the main idea of the proof in conversation with \emph{Astra}. The key insight consists of applying Yuan's equidistribution results, followed by a classification of $(f,f)$-preperiodic curves due to Pakovich and Beaumont followed by an additional application of equidistribution on a parametrized preperiodic curve.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Ferraguti, Carlo Pagano

item.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.16169v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We answer, in the trace metric, a question of Kowalski and Untrau on Wasserstein distances of all orders between the distribution $\mu_q$ of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and the Sato-Tate law $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$: we prove bounds for every order $s$ and show that their exponents are optimal for Katz-type moment bounds. In the trace metric we prove $W_s(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll_s q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s<3$, $W_3\ll q^{-1/3}(\log q)^{1/3}$, $W_s\ll_s q^{-1/4-1/(4s)}$ for $3<s<\infty$ and $W_\infty\ll q^{-1/4}$. In the angle metric we obtain bounds of every order, including $W_2\le 7q^{-1/3}$ and $W_\infty\ll q^{-1/6}$. These estimates follow from a general theorem for probability measures satisfying Katz-type Chebyshev moment bounds. Its proof combines an edge-sensitive discrepancy estimate with a new level-set bound for the distribution function and a quantile-displacement argument. We construct measures showing that the resulting exponents cannot in general be improved using moment bounds of this type alone, in the trace metric and in the angle metric for $s\le 2$ and $s\ge 6$ (up to logarithms); these constructions do not assert optimality for the Kloosterman measures themselves. A sharp comparison between Wasserstein distances and the Kolmogorov distance for the Sato-Tate law exhibits the same transition at $s=3$. Finally, using the exact third moment, we prove $W_1(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})>q^{-1/2}/10$ when $3\nmid q$.
item.dc:creator: Amir M. Rahimi

item.title: Weyl Bounds for $\operatorname{GL}_2\times \operatorname{GL}_2$ Rankin--Selberg $L$-functions via Short Spectral Moments
item.description: arXiv:2610.27804v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f$ and $g$ be Hecke--Maass cusp forms of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with spectral parameters $t_f$ and $t_g$, respectively. Let $T$ be a large parameter and put $L = |T-t_g|.$ We prove the Lindel\"of-on-average estimate \[ \sum_{ |t_f-T|\leq H} \left|L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right)\right|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon} T^{1+\varepsilon}H, \] uniformly in the range \[ T^{1/3+\varepsilon}\ll H,\qquad HT^\varepsilon\ll L\leq T. \] As an immediate consequence, in the generic range when both $|t_g|$ and $L$ are of size $T$, we obtain the Weyl bound \[ L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right) \ll_\varepsilon C(f\times g)^{1/6+\varepsilon}. \]
item.dc:creator: Zihao Wang

item.title: The Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of fixed even difference from a uniform zeta-ratios conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.32672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Hardy-Littlewood asymptotic for prime pairs of every fixed positive even difference $h$ from a restricted uniform two-over-two zeta-ratios formula. The formula may have error $O_\varepsilon(U^{\vartheta+\varepsilon})$ for any fixed $1/2\le\vartheta<(39-\sqrt{177})/32$. The real parts of all four shifts lie in $[3/64,5/64]$; their imaginary parts need only have absolute value at most $U^\nu$, for a fixed $0<\nu\le1/4$. For a fixed real smooth weight supported in $(1,1+1/(25h))$, we obtain an error $O_{h,W,\varepsilon}(x^{-\Delta(\vartheta)+\varepsilon})$ in the correlation sum with weight $W(n/x)^2/n$, where $\Delta(\vartheta)=7/16-\vartheta+\vartheta/(3-\vartheta)>0$. Adding the Riemann hypothesis improves this error to $O_{h,W,\varepsilon}(x^{\vartheta-7/8+\varepsilon})$. The proof retains the crossed zero residues in Mellin inversion and estimates their mixed term with the logarithmic-derivative integral. Two nonnegative time weights have the same diagonal term and opposite coefficients for the difference $h$. We deduce the logarithmic asymptotic for the weighted prime-pair sum $B_h$ and an asymptotic for the second finite difference of integrals of squared increments of the truncated Chebyshev function. The latter is connected to a logarithmically weighted M\"obius approximant in the Nyman-Beurling criterion by finite identities.
item.dc:creator: SeungJu Lee

item.title: Serre's conjectures for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38884v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The present article proves (assuming GRH and a minor technical result) the veracity of Serre's conjectures for the field $\Q(\sqrt{13})$. In doing so, we prove a ``reduction to level 1'' result that holds for any real quadratic field with narrow class number one. However we can only establish the needed base cases for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$.
item.dc:creator: Luis Dieulefait, Ariel Pacetti

item.title: Uniform estimates for the Erd\H{o}s-Moser equation and its analogue in arithmetic progressions
item.description: arXiv:2610.39315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Erd\H{o}s-Moser equation in arithmetic progressions, $\sum i^k=m^k$, where $i$ runs over the positive integers $i<m$ with $i\equiv b \pmod q$. We prove that a solution has at most $\lfloor k/\log 2+3/2\rfloor$ terms for all $k<10^{55}$, and at most $k/\log 2+5/2$ terms in general; this linear bound is best possible for real solutions and replaces the previously known exponential bound $(k+1)2^{2k+1}$. For $k=3$ we obtain a complete classification: solutions with exactly $n$ terms exist if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5\}$, and in each case there are infinitely many primitive solutions. For even exponents there are no solutions with three terms, and there are no solutions at all for $k=4$, for every $k=2^s\ge 4$, and for every even $k$ with $4\le k\le 24$. The key analytic input is a uniform estimate for the classical equation $1^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$: the real exponent $\kappa_m$ for which $1^\kappa+\dots+(m-1)^\kappa=m^\kappa$ satisfies $\kappa_m=\log 2\,(m-3/2-\gamma_m/m)$ with $0<\gamma_m<1/(8\log 2)$ for every $m\ge 3$. The proofs rest on a method based on centres of mass, Steiner's parallel-axis theorem and what we call the half-mass principle. The same framework identifies the constants of a general class of balance equations through the moments of a mass distribution: $3/2$ is a Steiner quotient, and $25/12-3\log 2=1/12-f''(\log 2)/2$ with $f(\lambda)=\lambda/(e^\lambda-1)$, whose Bernoulli expansion explains why this constant is so small.
item.dc:creator: Elham Mehdi-Nezhad, Amir M. Rahimi

item.title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.39908v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every prime $p$ and every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$, we prove that, for every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines an incidence matrix factorization with a projective-plane construction controlling line-intersection numbers modulo $p$. A separate geometric construction in characteristic two yields better explicit constants in certain cases, and also gives integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $\Omega_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.
item.dc:creator: Firdavs Rakhmonov, Chi Hoi Yip

item.title: The distribution of $\alpha\pi$ modulo one in $\mathbb{F}q(T)$: beyond Matom\"aki's exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.00623v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\alpha$ be an element of $\Fq((1/T))$ which is not in $\Fq(T)$. We ask how small $\nrm{\alpha\pi}$ can be made when $\pi$ runs over irreducible polynomials, and write $\theta(\alpha)$ for the largest exponent $\theta$ such that $\nrm{\alpha\pi}<|\pi|^{-\theta}$ has infinitely many solutions. The analogue of Matom\"aki's exponent, $\theta(\alpha)\ge\frac13$, was proved by Baier and the author, and it is the natural limit of \chg{methods based on} the Riemann Hypothesis. In this paper we go beyond it. For odd characteristic $p$ and $q$ large in terms of $p$ and $\theta$, we prove that $\theta(\alpha)\ge\theta$ for every $\alpha$ and every $\theta<\sqrt2-1=0.414\ldots$, and for every $\theta<\frac12$ when $\alpha$ has bounded partial quotients. The main tools are an exact count of points in affine subspaces of $\Fq[T]$, a splitting of these subspaces into long arithmetic progressions, and the results of Sawin and Shusterman on the M\"obius function along such progressions.
item.dc:creator: Esrafil Ali Molla

item.title: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.00647v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the pairs $(q,n)$, where $q$ is a prime power, $n>1$, and $\gcd(n,q)=1$, for which every irreducible factor of $\Phi_n(x)$ over $\F_q$ has exactly three nonzero terms. The positive support exponents of these factors have a common greatest common divisor, which gives a unique reduction by a power substitution. The reduced degree is two in odd characteristic and belongs to $\{2,3,4\}$ in characteristic two; the cubic and quartic cases arise by scalar substitution from the layers of orders $7$ and $15$. This yields necessary and sufficient arithmetic conditions on $(q,n)$ and explicit factorizations. Among the classified families, precisely those arising from quartic bases have a divisor layer containing an irreducible factor with more than three terms.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhu, Hongfeng Wu

item.title: On Shilov boundaries, Rees valuations and integral extensions
item.description: arXiv:2507.07091v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explore an analogy between, on one hand, the notions of integral closure of ideals and Rees valuations in commutative algebra and, on the other hand, the notions of spectral seminorm and Shilov boundary in nonarchimedean geometry. For any Tate ring $\mathcal{A}$ with a Noetherian ring of definition $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ and pseudo-uniformizer $\varpi\in\mathcal{A}_{0}$, we prove that the Shilov boundary for $\mathcal{A}$ naturally coincides with the set of Rees valuation rings of the principal ideal $(\varpi)_{\mathcal{A}_{0}}$ of $\mathcal{A}_{0}$. Furthermore, we characterize the Shilov boundary for a wide class of Tate rings by means of minimal open prime ideals in the subring of power-bounded elements. For affinoid algebras, in the sense of Tate, whose underlying rings are integral domains, this recovers a well-known result of Berkovich. Moreover, under some mild assumptions, we prove stability of our characterization of the Shilov boundary under (completed) integral extensions. In particular, for every mixed-characteristic Noetherian domain $R$, we obtain a description of the Shilov boundary for the Tate ring $\widehat{R^{+}}[p^{-1}]$, where $\widehat{R^{+}}$ is the $p$-adic completion of the absolute integral closure of the domain $R$.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine

item.title: The Golden Quadruple: Four Reals Whose Differences Form a Geometric Progression, Rigidity of the Golden Ratio, and a Bohr Almost Periodic Cosine Sum
item.description:
arXiv:2611.00973v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. The set $\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ is classical (Euclid, Elements XIII.8): by $\varphi^2=\varphi+1$ its six pairwise differences take the values $1,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3$, with multiplicities $1,2,2,1$. We write it as the golden quadruple $S=(F, F-a, F-b, F-a-b)$, $a=\varphi u$, $b=\varphi^2u$, $F>a+b$, and study its extremal and rigidity properties. No five distinct reals have all their positive differences in $\{u\varphi^n:n\in\mathbb{Z}\}$; this follows from a result of Lenstra (1977), and we give a self-contained proof. We give an elementary proof of uniqueness: every four-element set with this property is a translate of $u\varphi^m\{0,\varphi,\varphi^2,\varphi^3\}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$, and if all its differences lie in $\{u,\varphi u,\varphi^2u,\varphi^3u\}$ it is a translate of $S$. Among all $x>1$, only $x=\varphi$ admits a four-point set of reals whose set of distinct differences is $\{c,cx,cx^2,cx^3\}$. For the analogous quadruple with base $x
eq\varphi$ the failure is measured by two closure residues, which along Fibonacci quotients equal $\pm u/\mathrm{Fib}_n^2$ and $\pm \mathrm{Fib}_{n+1}u/\mathrm{Fib}_n^3$. The cosine sum $C_S(t)=\sum\cos(2\pi d t)$ over the six differences equals $8\cos^2(\pi a t)\cos^2(\pi b t)-2$; it is not periodic but is Bohr almost periodic, with explicit almost periods $	au_n=\mathrm{Fib}_n/u$, and we determine the two-term asymptotics $\sup_t|C_S(t+	au_n)-C_S(t)|=6\sqrt3 \pi\varphi^{-n}-2\sqrt3 \pi^3\varphi^{-3n}+O(\varphi^{-5n})$, with optimal constants; the inclusion length of the $\varepsilon$-almost periods is of order $1/\varepsilon$. For a scale $K>0$ the golden ladder $
u_n=K\varphi^{-n}$ realises the construction with differences $
u_{200},\dots,
u_{203}$; we evaluate it for $K=\sqrt{c^5/(Gh)}$. All proofs are elementary and self-contained.
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Przybylski
